title: The review deck — the layout you asked me to fix

steps.path: Two of your mascot questions, before and after this round
steps.headline: An explanation no longer looks like something you can pick, and every question says which one it is.
steps.changed: Before, the Today / The problem / Proposal blocks and the options you choose between were the same card — same fill, same border, same corners — so nothing said which ones you could click. Now an explanation is plain text behind a thin rule, and only a thing you can pick keeps a raised bordered card that lights up under the pointer. Each question also carries a QUESTION 1 OF 2 line, the gap between two questions is twice the gap inside one, and an answered question shows a green tick on that line.
steps.notice: You can tell at a glance what is a choice and what is background. Scrolling a long page, the numbered line tells you where you are without counting. Everything you read now starts on one left edge — the option letters used to push their words about 110 pixels further right than the paragraph above them.
steps.risk: The letter chip now sits on the same line as the option's title rather than in its own column. On a very narrow window the title wraps around it.

steps.path: The option cards, on a test deck
steps.headline: The same alignment and card treatment, on a question that sits beside a picture.
steps.changed: The option cards keep the raised fill and hover that mark them as choices, and their text lines up with the explanation above rather than indenting behind the letter.
steps.notice: Options read as a list you compare down a single edge instead of a row of boxes at different indents.
steps.risk: This is a test deck, so the words are placeholders. Judge the layout, not the content.

_comment: A RECORD, not a deck to rebuild. Its pictures came from scratch folders under /tmp that are gone; the answers beside it are what it decided. Re-serve with `serve --no-build` only if the run folders still exist.
